body.html: The Ritz-Carlton, Wolfsburg sits within the Autostadt, where the five-star hotel stands against an industrial backdrop. Luxury hospitality, automotive culture and a highly designed setting therefore meet in one place. Check-in marks the first direct transition from arrival to a guest’s personal stay. The room key card has a small but visible part in that moment: it is presented on arrival, carried throughout the stay and handled repeatedly. SFP’s direct commission addressed this touchpoint. The hotel required a genuine-leather holder and sought advice on its specification.

A key card holder needs to retain the card securely without making it awkward to remove. Its proportions and opening therefore begin with the card actually used by the hotel; edges and transitions also need to feel comfortable in repeated handling. Because the object is presented at close range during check-in, the leather surface, feel in the hand and precision of the branding carry particular weight.

SFP developed the specification directly with the hotel. On such a restrained object, the effect comes less from adding features than from proportion, material and carefully positioned branding. The card establishes the internal size; leather thickness, fold and edge construction determine how compactly the holder sits in the hand. The mark needs to be legible without crowding the small surface. The reception handover is part of the consideration too: staff should be able to pick up and present the holder naturally.

The hotel received a bespoke holder for an essential functional item. A loose room key card became an ordered, tactile part of the arrival experience. The genuine-leather piece carries the identity of the property while giving the guest a defined place for the card during the stay. Its value lies in the quality of this particular touchpoint: the function remains clear, while the material and execution relate to the hotel setting.
